newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZFOE to extend electricity futures contracts.
newsitem.headline: NZFOE to extend electricity futures contracts.

text.p: The New Zealand Futures and Options Exchange (NZFOE) is set to extend its range of electricity futures contracts to 12 months from six at present, manager of business development Greg Boland said on Tuesday.
Boland said the decision was taken in response to recent demand from market players.

He said the exchange was pleased with the level of demand for its Hayward reference contract. Liquidity and volume were both good, as evidenced by the number of trades and the tightness of the bid/ask spread.
He said the market was not drawing speculators at present but he was confident this would change.

""I think they will be drawn to something like this where there's high volatility," Boland said. Boland said the exchange had no plans to introduce a Benmore reference contract in the short term, as this would dilute volume, but would do so eventually if demand was sufficient.
"I think as people get more and more used to the benefits of using a futures market, they'll see there's a need to use these contracts in the South Island as well," Boland said.
Haywards and Benmore are the reference points for the North and South Islands respectively.
The NZFOE launched electricity futures contracts in November, a month after the launch of New Zealand's wholesale electricity market. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
